text:
sam: Heads up — Orion Health POC: customer hits 413 when uploading zipped clinical notes. Demo blocked. Error shows '413 Request Entity Too Large' immediately on PUT. Anyone seen this with presigned S3 uploads or multipart/form-data?

lee: Which flow — are they using our presign URL (S3 PUT) or uploading to our /uploads endpoint?

sam: They say presign -> client does PUT. Here's the failing curl (sanitized):
```
$ curl -v -X PUT "https://api.redwood.example/proxy/put/abcd1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/zip' -H 'Content-Length: 12582912' --data-binary @bundle.zip
```
Response: 413 from api.redwood.example (fast)

maya: Are they in which region? Hosted or dedicated? If we're seeing 413 from api.redwood.example the gateway is rejecting it, presigned PUT should go directly to S3 host (e.g., *.s3.amazonaws.com).

sam: Customer sent the presign URL — host looks suspicious: https://storage.redwood.example/upload/put?X-Amz-... — not an S3 host. Might be our proxying presign for some reason (legacy).

jordan: That explains it. If the presign URL points at our domain we're proxying the body through our gateway and the gateway 10MB limit triggers. For hosted we normally return a direct S3 URL. Two immediate fixes: 1) ensure presign returns real S3 host, or 2) increase gateway limit for this route (ops).

lee: Another common issue: client libs sometimes POST to our upload API instead of using the returned presign URL. Can you share the exact request trace (curl -v) showing the Host header and the full URL used by the client?

sam: Pasted the curl -v above. Host header is api.redwood.example. Customer says their mobile client uses a helper lib that did some rewrite — likely the root cause.

maya: Created ticket INC-2026-045 to collect full headers/traces. Quick workarounds: split file into smaller chunks, use S3 multipart uploads (recommended for >5MB parts), or reconfigure client to call the presigned S3 endpoint directly. Also avoid base64 in requests — it inflates size ~33%.

jordan: Long term: we can enable a higher gateway body limit for Orion if they sign the DPA / enterprise terms or move to Dedicated. Ops @deploy-bot can you open a gateway exception request for orion-poc-test?

deploy-bot: gateway-bot: Created GWE-4321 for orion-poc-test. Request queued — ETA ~2 hours for review.

lee: Also check CORS preflight — some browsers send OPTIONS to our domain which can complicate things. If the client is in-browser, presigned PUT should be to S3 with CORS configured on the bucket.

sam: Customer asked if gzipping before upload helps — yes, can reduce payload, but client needs to preserve correct Content-Type. They used base64 in a multipart JSON field which expanded size; switching to raw binary upload + multipart presign fixes it.

nina: On pricing: for their ask (approx 1TB/month of uploads + ~10k large puts) we should propose Dedicated reserved tier estimate + egress. I'll prepare a ballpark and follow up in this thread.

maya: For immediate unblock, recommend they: 1) verify client uses presigned S3 host (no api.redwood domain), 2) switch to multipart S3 upload for >5MB parts, or 3) temporarily split into <10MB chunks. We'll keep GWE-4321 open and update when gateway change completes.

sam: Thanks — I'll relay steps to customer and get their client logs/curl. Will update once they try the client fix. :thumbsup:
